clue.text: Out of practice, but try us anyway

indicators.note: done any way at all, so the letters of the two short words may fall in any order

explanation.surface: Someone is told to have a go even though they have not played for a while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'anyway' reads as 'regardless', but it tells you to rearrange TRYUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Skills that have not been used for a long time are said to have corroded like old metal.

clue.text: Mark of infamy in the style of a flower

definitions.text: in the style of a flower

explanation.surface: A badge of disgrace is described as being in a floral fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'style' is not fashion here: in botany the style is the stalk of the pistil, and the pollen-catching tip sits on top of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A mark of shame branded on someone, and also the pollen-receiving tip that sits on a flower's style.

clue.text: Ways to get round urban traffic problems

definitions.text: Ways to get round urban traffic problems

parts.words: Ways to get round urban traffic problems
parts.note: read as methods for solving congestion, but literally roads that go round a town to avoid its traffic

explanation.surface: A list of solutions for city congestion.
explanation.definitionFit: Ring roads built so through traffic need not enter a town centre are routes past the jams.

clue.text: An old campaigner who goes for the big fish?

definitions.text: who goes for the big fish?

explanation.surface: A veteran soldier turns angler after large catches.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes the word as someone who hunts the pike, a large freshwater fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A foot soldier of past wars armed with a long spear, and by a play on words an angler after the pike.

clue.text: Leading pointer in a sailing vessel

definitions.text: Leading pointer in a sailing vessel

parts.words: Leading pointer in a sailing vessel
parts.note: sounds like a navigator or compass aboard, but means the spar that literally points ahead from the front of the ship

explanation.surface: Asks for the chief guide aboard a sailing ship.
explanation.definitionFit: The spar projecting forward from a sailing ship's prow is the foremost thing pointing ahead.

clue.text: Tears, my, my! Obviously not in good shape

definitions.text: Tears, my, my! Obviously not in good shape

indicators.note: these words describe the fodder as badly formed, so its letters must be put into another order

explanation.surface: Someone cries out in dismay at something visibly misshapen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not in good shape' rearranges TEARSMYMY; the whole clue also describes the answer, a lack of balanced form.
explanation.definitionFit: Lack of balance between the two sides of something makes it visibly irregular in form.

clue.text: Truly, sir, one outcome of oppressive heat

indicators.note: what results from the words before is a new arrangement of their letters

parts.note: one is A, as in 'a' meaning a single thing

explanation.surface: A speaker politely agrees with a man that something results from stifling weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outcome of' rearranges TRULY, SIR and A (from 'one').
explanation.definitionFit: Heavy, humid atmosphere in close weather is the stifling warmth described.

clue.text: Unattached and morally undesirable

explanation.surface: Describes someone single and of doubtful virtue.
explanation.definitionFit: Free and not fastened down; also lax in morals, as in an old-fashioned 'woman of easy virtue'.

clue.text: Stimulate a dropout

indicators.note: out signals that the word before is in disorder, its letters to be reshuffled

explanation.surface: Encouraging someone who has abandoned their studies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropout' reads as one word for a quitter; split it and 'out' rearranges DROP.
explanation.definitionFit: To poke or urge someone into action is to spur them on.

clue.text: To be still isn't healthy

parts.note: reads as advice to keep active, but describes water or life turning foul from lack of movement

explanation.surface: A warning that sitting about is bad for you.
explanation.definitionFit: Standing water that does not flow goes foul, and a stagnant career or economy is likewise unhealthy.

clue.text: A summary ending acutely about backward Australian. natives

indicators.note: backward tells you to read the word for the Australian creatures from right to left

parts.note: emus are flightless birds native to Australia

explanation.surface: Describes a précis that closes sharply on some Australians.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ending acutely' points to the acute accent on the final E of the French-derived word for a summary.
explanation.definitionFit: A précis or brief account of a career, written with an acute accent on the last letter.

clue.text: Writer also Christian hardens Anne's resolution

indicators.note: a resolution is a working out, so the letters of the preceding words are worked into a new order

parts.note: here the S of the possessive is counted as a letter

explanation.surface: Anne grows more determined, and a writer is said to be a believer too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resolution' looks like Anne's determination; it rearranges HARDENSANNES. 'also Christian' points to the Danish fairy-tale writer's middle name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Danish author of The Little Mermaid was Hans Christian, so a writer whose name also includes Christian.

clue.text: See 12
Only card worth 2240 pounds at bridge?

definitions.text: Only card worth 2240 pounds at bridge?

parts.words: Only card worth 2240 pounds at bridge?
parts.note: the lone card of a suit held at bridge, read as one unit of 2240 pounds, a long ton

explanation.surface: Asks which bridge card could be so valuable.
explanation.walkthrough: A long ton, the British imperial ton, is 2240 pounds; read 'single ton' for a lone card held in a suit.
explanation.definitionFit: In bridge, a hand holding just one card of a suit is said to hold that card alone.

clue.text: Evidently doesn't have the edge

parts.note: reads as lacking an advantage, but literally describes something such as spectacles with no border

explanation.surface: Someone plainly lacks a competitive advantage.
explanation.definitionFit: Glasses or wheels without a surrounding frame or border are literally edgeless.

clue.text: Heroic Spartan lion sad in retreat

parts.note: Leo is Latin for lion and the lion of the zodiac

indicators.note: retreat means go backwards, so the two words before are read right to left

explanation.surface: A brave Greek warrior is pictured as a gloomy big cat backing away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lion' wants to be the definition beside 'Heroic Spartan', but it is the Latin and zodiac name for the beast; 'retreat' turns the next two words round.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spartan king who held the pass at Thermopylae against the Persians in 480 BC.

clue.text: Ancient coins, so they say

explanation.surface: A remark that old money is said to be so.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense treats the word as 'people who state', so those who state something say it.
explanation.definitionFit: Gold or silver coins of ancient Greece; and also people who declare, who say so.

clue.text: See 23
Take in a migrant bird

explanation.surface: Rescuing a bird that travels with the seasons.
explanation.definitionFit: To gulp something down, or believe it gullibly; and the fork-tailed bird that winters in Africa.

clue.text: Considerable number of Battle of Britain pilots?

explanation.surface: Asks whether the wartime airmen were numerous.
explanation.walkthrough: Churchill called the RAF fighter pilots of 1940 'the Few', so excellent ones are a fine few.
explanation.definitionFit: A colloquial phrase for quite a lot; and, punning on Churchill's 'the Few', the fine airmen of 1940.

clue.text: They're fruitful if backed by the Geographical Society

indicators.note: backed means turned round, so the little word before it is read in reverse

parts.note: GS is an abbreviation of Geographical Society

explanation.surface: A learned society is said to support productive ventures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' reverses only the little word before it; 'by' is a link joining the society's initials on.
explanation.definitionFit: Soft sweet Mediterranean fruits; plants that bear them are literally fruitful.

clue.text: River rodent loses its head

indicators.note: losing its head means the rodent's opening letter is dropped

parts.note: a mouse is a small rodent

explanation.surface: A small creature by the water is decapitated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loses its head' drops M from MOUSE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ouse is the name of several English rivers, notably in Yorkshire.

clue.text: Best, it's said, if you think about them

definitions.text: Best, it's said, if you think about them

parts.words: Best, it's said, if you think about them
parts.note: recalls the proverb that reconsidered opinions are best, and these are what you have when you think again

explanation.surface: Quotes a saying about reflection.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb runs '... are best': reconsidering a decision is wiser than acting on impulse.
explanation.definitionFit: Reconsidered ideas after reflection, the proverb says, are the wiser ones.

clue.text: Pledges pieces on board

explanation.surface: Promises are compared to the men on a chessboard.
explanation.definitionFit: Deposits with a lender as security; also the least valuable chessmen.

clue.text: Observant enough to recognise a gin cocktail

parts.note: to see something can mean to recognise or understand it

indicators.note: a cocktail is a mixture, so the letters of the spirit are mixed

explanation.surface: Someone sharp-eyed enough to identify a mixed drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'enough to' is a link phrase; 'cocktail' says the spirit's letters are mixed, not that a drink is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Able to perceive with the eyes, as opposed to blind; watchful.

clue.text: Reason with a Scot, an expert on the subject

parts.note: logic is the science of reasoning
Ian is a typical Scottish first name

explanation.surface: Arguing with a Scotsman who is an authority on the matter.
explanation.walkthrough: The subject is the logic just mentioned, so the definition leans on the clue's first word.
explanation.definitionFit: A specialist in the science of reasoning is an expert in that subject.

clue.text: White powdery substance an artist put in a container

indicators.note: put in means placed inside, so the artist goes into the container

parts.note: RA stands for a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A painter stores a white powder in a box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put in' says the artist goes inside the container; 'a' before 'container' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A white mineral salt, sodium borate, used in cleaning and as a flux.

clue.text: Temperate land mass

explanation.surface: Describes a moderate climate on a large area of land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Temperate' here means self-restrained, not mild in climate.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-restrained, exercising moderation; and one of the great divisions of land such as Asia.
